title: vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoored release
description: The vsftpd 2.3.4 source archive distributed in mid-2011 contained a backdoor that opens a root shell when a username ending in ':)' is sent.
remediation: Replace vsftpd with a current release from a trusted source and verify package signatures.

title: OpenSSH username enumeration
description: OpenSSH before 7.7 responds differently to valid and invalid usernames during public-key authentication, letting an attacker enumerate accounts before password attacks.
remediation: Upgrade OpenSSH to 7.7 or later, disable password authentication and rate-limit SSH.

title: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49 path traversal
description: A path normalisation flaw in Apache 2.4.49 allows files outside the document root to be read and, with mod_cgi enabled, remote code execution.
remediation: Upgrade to Apache 2.4.51 or later (2.4.50 fix was incomplete, see CVE-2021-42013) and set 'Require all denied' on the filesystem root.

title: Tomcat Manager application exposed
description: The Tomcat Manager is reachable from the network. It is a frequent target for default or weak credentials, after which a malicious WAR file can be deployed.
remediation: Restrict /manager to localhost or a management VLAN, remove default users from tomcat-users.xml and enforce strong credentials.

title: SMBv1 enabled (MS17-010 exposure)
description: SMBv1 is enabled. Unpatched hosts are exposed to MS17-010 (EternalBlue), which was used by WannaCry and NotPetya for wormable lateral movement.
remediation: Apply MS17-010, disable SMBv1 and block TCP 445 between workstation segments.

title: Telnet remote access in cleartext
description: Telnet sends credentials and session data unencrypted, so anyone on the network path can capture them.
remediation: Disable Telnet and use SSH with key-based authentication.

title: Redis accepts unauthenticated commands
description: Redis answered PING without authentication. Unauthenticated Redis can be abused to read data or write files such as SSH authorized_keys or cron jobs.
remediation: Bind Redis to localhost, enable protected-mode and requirepass or ACLs, and firewall port 6379.

title: RDP exposed to the network
description: Remote Desktop is reachable. Exposed RDP is a common target for password spraying and, on unpatched systems, for BlueKeep-class vulnerabilities.
remediation: Put RDP behind a VPN or RD Gateway, enforce NLA and MFA, and apply account lockout.

title: End-of-life MySQL server
description: MySQL releases before 5.7 no longer receive security fixes, so known vulnerabilities stay unpatched.
remediation: Upgrade to a supported MySQL release and restrict 3306 to application servers.

title: ProFTPD 1.3.5 mod_copy unauthenticated file copy
description: mod_copy in ProFTPD 1.3.5 lets unauthenticated users copy files with SITE CPFR/CPTO, which can be chained into code execution through the web root.
remediation: Upgrade ProFTPD and disable mod_copy if it is not needed.

title: Samba usermap_script command injection
description: When 'username map script' is configured, Samba 3.0.0 to 3.0.25rc3 passes unfiltered usernames to /bin/sh, allowing remote command execution.
remediation: Upgrade Samba to a supported release and remove the username map script option.

title: FTP advertises anonymous access
description: The FTP banner advertises anonymous login, which often exposes internal files or a writable upload directory.
remediation: Disable anonymous FTP or restrict it to a read-only, non-sensitive directory.
